messages:
customer-support: FYI — got an inbound escalation from AcmeCorp: API p99 went from ~300ms to ~1.6s in eu-west last 45m. Customers seeing timeouts.
lee: seeing spike on p99s in eu-west ingresses too, p95 up but p99 worst. Any recent rollouts?
marta: no prod deploys to edge control plane in last 2h. Alerting surfaced TLS handshake increase and SYN retransmits on some POPs.
lee: running quick probe: curl -v to api-redwood.eu-west from my laptop returns TLS handshake ~900ms. Traceroute shows cross-az hop.
net-eng: started looking at anycast mapping — noticing a subset of egress AS paths shifted to partner peer in front of us. Could be BGP flap causing hairpin.
nate: can you paste traceroute + tcpdump snippet? want to correlate with SNI -> edge mapping.
lee: here are probes (sanitized):
```
traceroute to api-redwood.eu-west (52.31.12.94), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.8.0.1  0.32 ms  0.29 ms  0.25 ms
 2  192.0.2.5  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.0 ms
 3  203.0.113.45  120 ms  118 ms  121 ms  <-- cross-region handoff
 4  52.31.12.94  910 ms  905 ms  908 ms
```
lee: tcpdump shows repeated retransmits during handshake and delayed FINs.
customer-support: Acme customer provided HAR — they hit websocket timeouts and 503s briefly.
marta: correlating logs: connection open -> TLS handshake start -> backend selection delayed ~700ms on route lookup. suspect geo-routing fallback path.
net-eng: confirmed — some DNS anycast shards returned stale glue, causing subset of clients to resolve to a farther POP in another AZ/region. TTLs were low but caching in ISP amplified.
nate: mitigation suggestions: 1) pin routes for affected prefix to eu-west core AS via temporary BGP preference, 2) reduce handshake timeout to fail faster and trigger local fallback, 3) sweep for stale glue and flush authoritative caches where possible.
lee: started a rolling route pin for affected AS via net-eng playbook, and issued internal DNS flush for our authoritative nameservers. Will monitor.
ops-bot: Deploy started: route-pin-eu-west-334123 (run_id: rp-334123). ETA ~90s.
marta: also enabling faster model fallback in edge proxy to avoid expensive route lookup during handshake — will lower selection SLO threshold for 10m.
net-eng: net changes applied, BGP preference updated. seeing traceroutes drop to ~80-120ms now.
lee: p99 for TLS handshake dropped from 1.6s -> 220ms in latest dashboard. p95 stable.
customer-support: updated Acme support thread: applied temporary mitigation, monitoring. They asked for RCA and ETA for full fix.
nate: next steps for RCA: gather BGP updates, authoritative DNS change timeline, ISP cache influence, and verify any downstream CDN caches.
marta: logging action items: (1) follow up with peering partner about stale glue (2) add alert for anomalous anycast shard divergence (3) test TTL hardening on staging NS for 48h.
lee: thanks team. if p99 climbs again, we'll revert fallback changes and open emergency call. :thumbsup:
customer-support: thanks, closing loop with customer for now.
